summary: Defines an extension to JMAP for Mail (RFC 8621) that returns the S/MIME signature verification status of a message. That lets a mail client show whether a signature checked out without doing the verification itself. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: A mail server tells your mail app whether the signature on a letter is real.

questions: how to check s/mime signature in jmap
how does jmap report s/mime signature status
what does signed/verified mean in jmap
how long can a jmap server cache s/mime verification
subtitle: Lets a JMAP mail server tell your mail client whether an S/MIME signature checked out, so the client does not have to.

tldr.problem: To check an S/MIME signature, a JMAP client would have to download the signature part and all signed body parts, or download and decode the CMS data itself.
tldr.mechanism: The server verifies the signature and reports the result through new Email/get properties such as smimeStatus and smimeErrors, plus new Email/query filters.
tldr.outcome: Clients save bandwidth and code complexity, but must trust the server's verification code, configuration and operational practices.

today: RFC 9219 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2022. It has not been obsoleted or updated, so it is still the definition of this JMAP extension.

sections.title: Why Verify on the Server
sections.content:
JMAP for Mail (RFC 8621) is a JSON-based protocol for synchronizing email between a client and a server. RFC 9219 adds an extension that returns the S/MIME signature verification status of a message (S/MIME itself is specified in RFC 8551).

Without it, a client has to download the signature body part and all signed body parts (for multipart/signed), or download and decode the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) data (for application/pkcs7-mime). With the extension, the server does that work and the client just reads a result.

Using the extension means the client trusts the server's S/MIME verification code and configuration. The RFC says it suits cases where saving bandwidth and client-side code outweighs that concern, for example when one organization controls both the server and the client.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of every kid checking the teacher's signature on a note, the school office checks it once and tells everybody the answer.

sections.title: Advertising the Capability
sections.content:
Servers that support the extension MUST add a property called urn:ietf:params:jmap:smimeverify to the capabilities object of the JMAP Session object (see RFC 8620). The value is an empty object, both in the Session capabilities property and in an account's accountCapabilities property.

A client that sees this capability knows it can ask for the new properties and use the new filters.
sections.plainLanguage: The server hangs a sign on its door saying 'I can check signatures here', so the app knows it may ask.

sections.title: New Email/get Properties
sections.content:
The extension defines four properties that a client can request in the properties argument of Email/get:

  • smimeStatus: the current verification status. It is a string, or null when the message has no signature.
  • smimeStatusAtDelivery: the same value calculated as of the receivedAt date and time. It does not change unless trust anchors are added, so a client can compare it with the current status to answer 'was the signature valid at delivery?'.
  • smimeErrors: an array of human-readable problem descriptions, or null when there is no signature or no errors. It is non-null only when the status is signed/failed or encrypted+signed/failed.
  • smimeVerifiedAt: the date and time the signature was most recently verified, or null if there is no signature or no verification was attempted.

The server can defer calculating smimeStatusAtDelivery until it is asked for, but once calculated it remembers the value.
sections.plainLanguage: Your app can ask four questions about a letter: is the seal good now, was it good when the letter arrived, what is wrong with it, and when did you last check?

sections.title: The smimeStatus Values
sections.content:
The defined smimeStatus values are:

  • unknown: an S/MIME message that was neither signed nor encrypted. It can also be returned for a multipart/signed message with an unrecognized signing protocol, for example OpenPGP.
  • signed: signed, but not yet verified. Some servers wait until a message is requested. Compliant servers SHOULD attempt verification and return signed/verified or signed/failed instead.
  • signed/verified: the signature verified according to RFC 8551 and RFC 8550, and the signer email address in the certificate matches the From header field. The signer certificate SHOULD be checked for revocation.
  • signed/failed: the signature failed to verify, for example because of a policy decision such as an address mismatch, a modified message, or an expired or revoked certificate.
  • encrypted+signed/verified and encrypted+signed/failed: reserved for future use, typically handled like signed/verified and signed/failed.

Servers MAY return other values defined by extensions. Clients MUST treat unrecognized values as unknown or signed/failed. All values MUST be ASCII, since they are tokens and not localized text. The value can also change over time.
sections.plainLanguage: The answer is one of a few words, like 'good seal', 'bad seal', 'not checked yet' or 'not a sealed letter'. If your app sees a word it does not know, it should be careful and treat it as not trusted.

sections.title: Searching, Caching and Change Tracking
sections.content:
Email/query gets three new FilterCondition properties, all Booleans. hasSmime matches messages whose smimeStatus is not null (true) or null (false). hasVerifiedSmime matches messages whose status is signed/verified or encrypted+signed/verified. hasVerifiedSmimeAtDelivery works the same way but uses smimeStatusAtDelivery. Using hasVerifiedSmime can be expensive, because the server must calculate the status for every message.

Recalculating statuses is costly, so the server MAY cache smimeStatus and smimeErrors for up to 24 hours; smimeVerifiedAt records when they were last updated.

For Email/changes, a change to smimeVerifiedAt alone MUST NOT put a message in the updated list. A change to smimeStatus, smimeStatusAtDelivery or smimeErrors MUST.
sections.plainLanguage: You can ask the server to find only the signed letters, or only the ones with good seals. It may reuse an answer for up to a day, and it only shouts 'something changed!' when the answer changes, not when it merely rechecks.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The client must trust the server's verification code, configuration and operational practices, and must trust that the channel to the server is integrity protected. The RFC points to TLS, which JMAP requires (RFC 8620, Section 8.1). A server missing some trust anchors will report signed/failed for messages that would otherwise verify.

A malicious or compromised server could report success for a forged or altered message, or report failure, or no signature, for a properly signed one. The second attack adds nothing beyond what such a server could already do by stripping or tampering with the S/MIME data. The first can be detected by client software that does its own verification, if local configuration enables it.

Constantly recalculating signature status can cause a denial-of-service condition, so servers are RECOMMENDED to cache results for up to 24 hours.
sections.plainLanguage: If you let the office check seals for you, you have to trust the office. A dishonest office could lie, so careful apps can double-check.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: IANA has registered the JMAP capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:smimeverify. The registration names RFC 9219 as the specification, gives the intended use as common, lists the IETF as change controller, and points to Section 6 of this RFC for security and privacy considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The name of the new feature was written in the official list so nobody else uses it.

items.desc: Signature verified and signer address matches From.
